questions.question: How does DUO's decoding strategy differ fundamentally from the time-division approach used by MiniCPM-Duplex?

options.A: DUO processes input and output simultaneously on separate channels, while MiniCPM-Duplex splits and mixes them sequentially in time slices
options.B: DUO alternates full forward passes, while MiniCPM-Duplex uses a single parallel pass
options.C: DUO changes the training corpus into time slices, while MiniCPM-Duplex preserves channel separation
options.D: DUO generates input and output with separate models, while MiniCPM-Duplex shares a single autoregressive model

questions.rationale: DUO modifies decoding to run input prefill/prediction alongside output autoregression, whereas MiniCPM-Duplex changes the data/model format to time-division multiplexing.
questions.evidence_quote: In contrast, DUO processes the input and output simultaneously by optimizing the decoding strategy

questions.question: What attention-mask constraint prevents the newly generated input and output continuations from contaminating each other's language modeling?

options.A: After the new input arrives, tokens in the input and output channels do not attend to each other's subsequent tokens
options.B: All output tokens attend bidirectionally to every future input token
options.C: Input tokens attend only to the final output token and never to shared prefixes
options.D: The mask blocks both channels from attending to any prefix token

questions.rationale: The channels share prefix tokens but their post-arrival continuations remain isolated by the modified causal mask.
questions.evidence_quote: the tokens generated by the input and output channels after t1 do not attend to each other

questions.question: What do DUO's two state tokens mean for channel transition?

options.A: <1> marks a user query and promotes input to the output channel; <2> marks non-query text to discard
options.B: <1> marks background text to ignore; <2> suspends output and answers the input
options.C: <1> terminates the output; <2> restarts the model from its initial prompt
options.D: <1> indicates the assistant is speaking; <2> indicates a user interruption

questions.rationale: The state tokens direct whether to answer or ignore the newly processed input, and determine which channel continues as output.
questions.evidence_quote: State token <1> denotes that the input is a user query.

questions.question: Why does DUO maintain the existing output channel after processing new input until a state token is encountered or generation ends?

options.A: The incoming text may be non-query background, so the model must continue answering the original request unless the input is classified as a query
options.B: The model cannot pause decoding without discarding its entire KV cache
options.C: The output channel must finish every response before it can inspect user input
options.D: The state token is generated only after the original output reaches its length limit

questions.rationale: This behavior allows the assistant to keep responding when the newly received speech is not a query, while enabling transition when it is.
questions.evidence_quote: This output channel is maintained until either the model responds to the new query or the output sequence is completed.

questions.question: How does the training-data construction support DUO's minimal-training design?

options.A: Convert Duplex-UltraChat to turn-based data, append <1> to answerable user content, and add ChatGPT-generated context-relevant non-query text
options.B: Retain Duplex-UltraChat's time-sliced format and train without state tokens
options.C: Generate all assistant answers with ChatGPT and remove user turns from training
options.D: Use only non-query inputs, assigning <2> to every user message

questions.rationale: The paper converts the source to standard turn-based format, labels response-requiring queries, and synthesizes non-query inputs for the ignore behavior.
questions.evidence_quote: Since all queries in the dataset require a response, we append the <1> token to each user’s content.

questions.question: What were the scale and compute cost of DUO training compared with the cited MiniCPM-Duplex training?

options.A: 10K samples, 400 steps on 8 A100s for about 25 minutes versus about 5,000K samples, 10,000 steps on 40 A100s for 36 hours
options.B: 5,000K samples, 400 steps on 40 A100s for 36 hours versus 10K samples on 8 A100s for 25 minutes
options.C: 10K samples, 10,000 steps on 8 A100s for 36 hours versus 5,000K samples for 25 minutes
options.D: Both used 10K samples and 400 steps, but DUO used twice as many GPUs

questions.rationale: The setup reports the dataset size, steps, GPU count, and runtime for both systems, illustrating the reduced training cost.
questions.evidence_quote: MiniCPM-Duo is trained for 400 steps on 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs for about 25 minutes.

questions.question: What loss is used during DUO training, and how many predicted input-channel tokens are processed per cycle?

options.A: Loss on state tokens and output; α=4 input-channel tokens
options.B: Loss on all input and output tokens; α=1 token
options.C: Loss only on state tokens; α=10 input-channel tokens
options.D: Contrastive loss on channel states; α=2 output tokens

questions.rationale: The training setup specifies loss on state tokens plus output, and the input prediction horizon α is set to four.
questions.evidence_quote: The loss is calculated on the state tokens and output.

questions.question: Which human-evaluation dimensions did the authors use, and how was the dialogue material obtained?

options.A: Responsiveness, human-likeness, faithfulness, and factuality; 40 multi-turn sessions per model were recorded in a voice demo
options.B: Accuracy, toxicity, latency, and fluency; 400 written prompts were judged automatically
options.C: Responsiveness and factuality only; one session per annotator was used
options.D: Faithfulness and coherence only; benchmark prompts were translated into audio

questions.rationale: The evaluation adapts a voice demo, records 40 multi-turn interactions with each model, and ranks dialogue quality on four named axes.
questions.evidence_quote:
Following Zhang et al. (2024)’s work, we con-
sider four aspects: responsiveness, human-likeness,
faithfulness, and factuality.

questions.question: How did DUO compare with MiniCPM-Duplex on standard benchmarks after limited duplex training?

options.A: It remained broadly comparable to both the original MiniCPM and the Duplex baseline, with several scores recovering relative to the 10K-trained Duplex variant
options.B: It substantially outperformed the original model on every benchmark
options.C: It lost performance on every benchmark because channel separation disrupts language modeling
options.D: It matched Duplex only on math but was not evaluated on reasoning or code

questions.rationale: Table 1 shows comparable performance overall; the authors also note the undertrained Duplex model's scores drop while DUO preserves more base capability.
questions.evidence_quote:
MiniCPM-Duo achieves comparable re-
sults with MiniCPM-Duplex and MiniCPM.

questions.question: What is the main stated limitation of the evaluation scope, and what extension do the authors propose?

options.A: Experiments focus primarily on language models; they propose extending DUO to multimodal inputs encoded as tokens
options.B: The study evaluates only English text and proposes translating the model to Bangla
options.C: The system is tested only on batch benchmarks, so the authors propose adding voice interaction
options.D: The evaluation lacks state tokens, so future work will replace them with time slices

questions.rationale: The limitations section flags multimodal generalization and suggests feeding encoder-derived modality features as input tokens.
questions.evidence_quote: The experiments primarily focused on language models, potentially limiting the generalizability of ﬁndings to other domains.
